data.scenario_text: You stand <m>55</m> feet from the point on the ground directly below a kite. The angle of elevation from your feet to the kite is <m>40^\circ</m>.
data.find_task: Find the height of the kite above the ground. Do not round until the final answer; then round to two decimal places as necessary.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). A correct sketch shows a right triangle with the right angle marked, the given 40^\circ angle placed at the correct vertex, and the one given length written on its correct side: the leg adjacent to the given angle is 55\text{ ft}. The other two side lengths are not given, so they stay unlabeled. The 40^\circ angle belongs at your feet on the ground, between the horizontal ground and the line of sight to the kite. It is an interior angle of the triangle as stated, so no conversion is needed.

Part (b). The angle of elevation is measured upward from the horizontal ground at your feet, which is already a vertex of the right triangle, so it is an interior angle as given -- no conversion is needed.

Read the triangle from that angle: the height of the kite above the ground is the leg opposite the given angle, and the known quantity is the leg adjacent to the given angle. The one basic ratio that uses exactly those two sides is tangent, \tan\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}, so that is the ratio to use.

Substituting and computing, h=55\tan(40^\circ).

So the height of the kite above the ground is \boxed{46.15\text{ ft}}.
